knowledge-base.name: branching-strategy
knowledge-base.triggers: git, branch, branching, pull request, PR, merge, commit, cherry-pick, rebase, feature branch, sprint-release, patch-release, hotfix, conventional commits, Jira ticket, workflow, backport, release branch, team branch
knowledge-base.overview: Team-specific three-tier branching strategy: trunk (main/master) receives PR merges only from release branches (sprint-release-##, patch-release-##, hotfix-yyyymmdd), which receive PR merges only from short-lived feature branches ([type]/TICKET-short-desc). Direct commits to team branches are forbidden, even for already-approved cherry-picks.

tier.name: trunk
tier.accepts: PR merges from sprint-release-##, patch-release-##, hotfix-yyyymmdd only
tier.forbidden: Direct commits, force pushes, feature branches merging directly

tier.name: release
tier.accepts: PR merges from feature branches only
tier.forbidden: Direct commits (even for cherry-picks of approved code)
tier.purpose: sprint-release-## accumulates the current sprint's work before release to main. patch-release-## accumulates bug fixes for a patch release on top of a prior main. hotfix-yyyymmdd handles urgent production fixes dated by the hotfix day.

tier.name: feature
tier.protection: none, short-lived, owned by one developer
tier.accepts: direct commits from the owning developer
tier.lifetime: ideally under 3 days, delete immediately after PR merge

naming-convention.rule: Jira ticket ID must be uppercase with correct project key (e.g. PROJ-456, not proj-456)
Description is lowercase, hyphen-separated, 3 to 5 words
Type prefix must match a conventional commit type: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, perf, ci

conventional-commits.types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, perf, ci

subject-rules.rule: No capital letter at the start of description

body-rules.rule: Jira ticket ID goes on its own line in the body, not in the subject
Explain the why, not the what

conventional-commits.code-example:
feat(auth): add multi-factor authentication flow
Implements TOTP-based MFA for neighbor sign-in. Users can enroll a device during registration or from account settings.
PROJ-456
conventional-commits.bad-reason: Ticket ID in subject, past tense, capital letter, trailing period, no body explanation.

pull-request-governance.check: Target branch is correct: feature targets sprint-release-##; cherry-pick targets patch-release-## or hotfix-yyyymmdd
Source branch follows [type]/TICKET-description naming with uppercase project key
PR description follows team template (Description, Jira Ticket, Type, Tests, Checklist)
Minimum 1 team review plus Tech Lead approval before merge (exception: self-merge of pre-approved cherry-pick)
Branch is rebased on latest target, conflicts resolved locally
Tests pass locally and in CI
pull-request-governance.rule: Never commit directly to main, master, sprint-release-*, patch-release-*, or hotfix-* — even for already-approved cherry-picks. Every change to a team branch must arrive via a visible PR.
Never force-push to a shared or protected branch.
A cherry-pick PR targets the release branch it is backporting into, NOT main/master.

pr-template.section: Brief summary of what changed and why.
feat / fix / docs / refactor / chore / perf / ci / test / style
What was tested and how (locally, in staging, regression suite).

scenario.name: cherry-pick-into-patch-branch
scenario.when: A bug fix already approved and merged on sprint-release-## needs to ship via an earlier patch-release-##

steps.step: Resolve conflicts if any, run tests locally
Self-merge: no second review required since the code was already approved on sprint-release-##, but the PR itself must still exist as a visible record
Delete the feature branch after merge

scenario.anti-pattern: Committing the cherry-pick directly to patch-release-## to "save time". Shane's exact correction on PE PR #437: "You shouldn't really commit directly to any of our team branches, even if you know you're going to merge something that was already approved." The rule is about visibility and audit trail, not about re-review.

Opening the cherry-pick PR against main/master instead of patch-release-##. The patch release branch is the ship vehicle; main only sees the patch contents after patch-release-## itself merges to main.

scenario.name: hotfix-from-production
scenario.when: A critical bug is in production and needs to ship before the next sprint release

steps.step: Create feature branch fix/TICKET-description off hotfix-yyyymmdd
Implement fix, PR into hotfix-yyyymmdd, review, merge
PR hotfix-yyyymmdd into main/master once tested
Mirror the fix into sprint-release-## and any active patch-release-## so it isn't lost in the next release

cross-repo-coordination.note: PantryEasy (PE) and Nectar are often on different release schedules. Changes that cross both repos require mirroring.
cross-repo-coordination.rule: If a Nectar change depends on a PE change, the PE change must land on PE's patch-release-## so PE can ship independently when Nectar deploys.
Mirror the same change into PE's sprint-release-## too, so the next full release carries the fix and it gets exercised in all environments.
When opening the PR in PE, double-check the target branch — it's easy to land on master by default when the intended target is patch-release-##.

row.name: [type]/TICKET-*
row.deletion: as soon as the PR merges

anti-patterns.anti-pattern: Direct commits to main, master, sprint-release-*, patch-release-*, hotfix-*
Cherry-pick PR targeting main when it should target patch-release-##
Force push to a shared or protected branch
Merging without a PR (even a pre-approved cherry-pick still needs a visible PR)
Long-lived feature branches (over 3 days) that drift from the target branch
Multiple unrelated features or tickets in a single branch or PR
Lowercase project key in branch or commit (fix/proj-456 instead of fix/PROJ-456)
Jira ticket ID in commit subject line instead of body
Past-tense or capitalized commit subjects ("Added feature." instead of "add feature")
Skipping the PE mirror for a Nectar-PE cross-repo change

checklist.name: before-opening-pr
checklist.item: Correct target branch (feature -> sprint-release-##, cherry-pick -> patch-release-##, hotfix -> hotfix-yyyymmdd)
Branch name follows [type]/TICKET-description format with uppercase project key
Commit messages follow conventional commits with Jira ticket in body
Rebased on latest target branch, conflicts resolved locally
PR description follows the team template
If cross-repo: PE mirror PR identified or opened

decision-guide.name: where-does-this-change-go
decision-guide.question: Is this an urgent production bug that can't wait for the next sprint release?
decision-guide.yes: hotfix-yyyymmdd path, then mirror into active sprint-release and patch-release branches.

no.question: Is this a fix that needs to ship via a patch release (between sprints)?
no.yes: Feature branch off patch-release-##, PR into patch-release-##. If the fix is already merged on sprint-release-##, cherry-pick via a feature branch + PR.
no.no: Normal sprint work: feature branch off sprint-release-##, PR into sprint-release-##.
